the control of the pulse-modes of guided quantum states by means integrated nonlinear optical devices.
the fundamental understanding of the spatiotempral structure of quantum states, and with the development of integrated optical components for their manipulation and control.

our work opens up a novel and powerful route for the complete control of quantum light pulses, which is of great interest in the context of quantum information and quantum communication.
our results provide a solid basis for future applications of quantum frequency conversion for quantum information processing and quantum metrology.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of QPGs and QPSs allows for a full control over the pulse-mode structure and, thus, the spatiotemporally structured quantum states of light.
, by means of integrated optical pulse shaper-engineering, we have developed a new route towards full control over the pulse-mode structure in nonlinear waveguides.
, with the use of integrated nonlinear optics, the inherent pulse-moded nature of ultrafast pulse quantum states can be fully exploited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pulse-mode structure can be controlled with high fidelity, which is a key ingredient for future quantum information applications.
nonlinear integrated optics can be used to generate and shape the spectral mode structure of pulsed quantum states, and that these concepts can be generalized to arbitrary quantum processes.
the QPG and QPS can be used to tailor the spatiotemporally shaped output of a quantum frequency conversion process, which is of high interest in quantum information processing and quantum metrology.
